summary: The 76-episode Bobobo-bo Bo-bobo TV series adapts manga chapters (奥義) 1-178 of 230, i.e. volumes 1 through the front of volume 17, stopping partway into the Reverse-Maruhage / Dark-Emperor (闇皇帝編) arc - ja.wikipedia states flatly that the anime covers 原作の「闇皇帝編」途中まで. No source anywhere publishes a per-episode chapter map for this series (the fandom episode pages carry no 'manga counterpart' field and there are no per-chapter pages), so this lattice is a derivation built by cross-matching four independent layers: en.wikipedia's full per-episode synopses, en.wikipedia's chapter list (Japanese titles + volume boundaries), bobobo.fandom's per-episode 'Major Events' and 'Changes from the manga' sections, and bobobo.fandom's character/location infobox debut pairs (Debut (Manga) = Chapter N / Debut (Anime) = Episode M) - with the ja.wikipedia and Toei-official Japanese subtitles as a fifth check, since many episode subtitles quote chapter titles verbatim. The structural find that makes the back half reliable: from ep 52 the show switched to a two-segment A/B-part format, and from ep 52 to ep 71 the adaptation runs at a strict, unbroken 2 chapters per episode (A-part = one chapter, B-part = the next), landing exactly on the volume boundaries at eps 54 (130), 60 (142) and 71 (164); eps 72-75 then accelerate to 3-4 chapters each. Pacing before that is looser (1-4 chapters per episode) and eps 2-3 are played out of manga order. The finale question is resolved in favour of the stored value: ep 76 does adapt ch 178, so END 178 / continue 179.

annotations.note: Ch 2 is split: its opening Maruhage block-leaders' conference cold-opens ep 1 (fandom A-Block infobox: former base Chapter 2 / Episode 1), while the rest of ch 2 (Killalino and Takashi) is deferred to ep 3.

The anime swaps the pair: ep 2 plays ch 4-5 (Christmas duel with Don Patch, then the wig-wearing H-Block platoon and Maitel) and ep 3 goes BACK to ch 2-3 (Killalino, then the Hajike Festival). bobobo.fandom's ep-2 page states it outright - 'A major difference from the manga is that this happened after the events of episode 3' - and the ep-3 page adds 'In the manga, Bo-bobo and Beauty meet Killalino before approaching Hajike Village and after taking down G-Block'. Ep 3 is therefore left unanchored rather than carrying a backwards END.

Dengakuman is introduced on the tag of ep 16, immediately after Jelly Jiggler's defeat. bobobo.fandom's ep-16 'Changes from the manga': 'Dengakuman is introduced almost immediately after Tennosuke's defeat, whereas the manga does not reveal him until the Z-Block invasion' - his manga debut is ch 59 (fandom Dengakuman infobox: Chapter 59 / Episode 16). The ep 16 anchor (END 34) is NOT inflated to 59.

bobobo.fandom's ep-24 'Changes from the manga': 'In the manga, Robo-Block and their beach resort was its own section of the Empire; the anime condenses it and makes it Z-Block's entrance area.' A compression, not a cut - ch 57's beach material is still animated.

bobobo.fandom's ep-60 'Changes from the manga' notes 'Rice appears earlier in the anime than in the manga' - the backup call that in the manga lands in ch 141-142 is brought forward slightly inside the episode. Does not move the END.

The finale stops inside the castle-raising beat rather than at an arc end: en.wikipedia's ep-76 synopsis covers Denbo's 'picture activity book' (ch 177 'Picture Book Paradise'), Hydrate's floating castle emerging, and the allies-and-enemies charge upward (ch 178 'Let's Go Everyone Showdown! Dark vs. Us'), then has the cast 'realize that this is the last episode'. bobobo.fandom's ep-76 Major Events additionally records Tsuru Tsurulina IV abdicating 'never to return', an anime-side send-off appended to that stopping point. Manga continues from ch 179.

structure.notes: One cumulative season of 76 TV episodes (TV Asahi, 2003-11-08 to 2005-10-29); our numbering already matches ja.wikipedia, Toei's official episode list, bobobo.fandom's episode list and animefillerlist one-for-one (verified title-by-title; the only differences are alternate English titles at eps 53, 56, 57 and 72, same Japanese subtitles). Chapter space: the mainline 奥義 numbering 1-230 across 21 tankobon - ja.wikipedia gives 第1部：全230話 and en.wikipedia's chapter list enumerates exactly 230 chapters with volume boundaries identical to the ones already stored (v1 1-10 ... v17 176-186). The stored anchor ep76 -> 178 is in that space and is CORRECT. Format change: eps 1-51 carry a single subtitle; from ep 52 each episode carries separate A-part and B-part subtitles (ja.wikipedia: 第52話からはAパートとBパートそれぞれにサブタイトルが付けられ2本立て形態に変更された). Adaptation cadence: ~1-4 chapters/episode through ep 51 (slowest at ep 11, a single chapter; fastest at eps 16, 20, 21, 23, 24, 27-30), then an unbroken exactly-2-chapters-per-episode run from ep 52 (ch 125-126) to ep 71 (ch 163-164), then 3, 3, 4, 2, 2 for eps 72-76. AFL types all 76 episodes Manga Canon, matching the stored typing - no filler, no anime-only rows, so A1 is not in play anywhere in this series.
order_only: 総集編 (recap special, aired 2004-10-23 between eps 32 and 33; a clip show in which the cast holds a meeting about the programme). It is outside the 76-episode count, carries no manga content, and was moved to a DVD bonus on VOL.12 - correctly absent from our 76 rows.

flags_for_sean: FINALE 177 vs 178 - RESOLVED in favour of 178 (no repair needed; the stored ep76 -> 178 is right). The '177' claim is a single sentence on bobobo.fandom's chapter-list page ('The last chapter adapted in the anime is Chapter 177, so after watching the anime, start at Chapter 178'), and it is contradicted by three independent lines of evidence: (1) en.wikipedia's ep-76 synopsis describes ch 177 content (Denbo forcing the enemy through a 'picture activity book' = 絵本パラダイス) AND ch 178 content (Hydrate's floating castle emerging, then 'Bo-bobo and his allies ally with friends and enemies as they race upwards towards their enemy' = 行くぜ全面対決!闇VSオレら); (2) the same fandom wiki's own Yamiking page gives Debut (Manga) = Chapter 178 / Debut (Anime) = Episode 76, and the ep-76 page lists 'The Yamiking rises from the Dark Realm with Hydrate' as a major event; (3) ja.wikipedia states the anime adapted 原作の「闇皇帝編」途中まで (partway INTO the Dark Emperor arc), which begins with that castle-raising. The Yahoo Chiebukuro answer cited in the prior pass ('up to okugi 178') agrees, and wheredoestheanimeleaveoff.com - content-farm, cross-check only - says to resume at vol 17 ch 179, which is END 178 + 1. Verdict: ep 76 END = 178, continue = 179, so no continue_point row is needed. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Bobobo-bo_Bo-bobo_episodes | https://bobobo.fandom.com/wiki/Yamiking | https://bobobo.fandom.com/wiki/Finally!_The_Final_Fight_of_Finality!_This_Time_We_Mean_It! | https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ボボボーボ・ボーボボ | (contra) https://bobobo.fandom.com/wiki/List_of_Bobobo-bo_Bo-bobo_manga_chapters

Open flag #709 (count_mismatch, MU latestChapter 40 vs AniList 230) - answerable: the reading edition is the 21-volume / 230-chapter Japanese tankobon numbering (奥義 1-230). ja.wikipedia gives 全303話 split as 第1部：全230話 / 第2部：全73話 (the sequel Shinsetsu restarts its own chapter and volume count at 1 and must never be folded in), and en.wikipedia's chapter list enumerates exactly 230 chapters with volume boundaries identical to the stored ones. MU's 40 is not the reading edition and should not be trusted for this title.

Tier caveat (hikaru lesson): the existing ep-76 anchor is source 'mu'. I am proposing no change to it, but if the apply step writes anything to that row it must flip the row to 'manual' or the next mu re-derive will erase it.

Honesty note on method: no published per-episode chapter map exists for this series. bobobo.fandom's episode pages have no manga-counterpart field, there are no per-chapter wiki pages (only one, 'Hajike Festival (Chapter)'), animefillerguide has no Bobobo entry, and searches in both English and Japanese turned up nothing beyond arc-level statements. Every anchor here is a cross-source derivation, not a quoted mapping. The high-confidence ones rest on an episode-title-to-chapter-title identity or two independent content matches; the medium ones rest on cadence plus one content match. Eps 40-42 are the weakest stretch (ep 41 is the only single-chapter anchor after ep 11 and the 40/41/42 split could shift by one chapter), and eps 17/18 could shift by one chapter at their shared boundary.

Ep 3 is deliberately left without an anchor. Its true content is ch 2-3, which is BEHIND ep 2's ch 4-5; anchoring it would put a backwards END into the series. The rearrangement is recorded as an annotation instead, and a reader who has finished ep 3 has in fact seen everything through ch 5.
